statement: Companhia de Vinhos dos Profetas e dos Villões is the Madeira and Porto Santo wine project of António Maçanita and Nuno Faria; the producer describes the project as arising from Faria's challenge to Maçanita during the beginning of the pandemic.

The producer's own history places the beginning of the broader Profetas e Villões collaboration around the beginning of the pandemic rather than establishing a precise 2021 founding date for the entire project.
The 2022 Listrão dos Profetas is a Porto Santo white wine made from Listrão from vines older than 80 years on limestone sandy-loam soils and released under D.O. Madeirense.

For 2022 Listrão dos Profetas, the producer documents manual harvest, whole-bunch direct pressing with three press fractions, no sulfur dioxide until the end of fermentation, pre-oxidation, spontaneous fermentation, and 11 months on lees in small stainless vessels and 228-litre barrels.

The 2023 Vinho da Corda dos Profetas is a Porto Santo wine from Listrão and Caracol, made from the final richer press fraction and released under D.O. Madeirense; the producer records 1,288 numbered bottles for this vintage.

The producer describes vinho da corda as a historical pre-fortification method in which the clearer first press fraction was separated from the richer, darker final press fraction called vinho da corda.

Portuguese regulatory authority treats DOP Madeirense and DOP Madeira as distinct protected designations; DOP Madeira is the fortified Madeira category, while the Profetas Porto Santo still wines are labeled D.O. Madeirense.

resolution_needed: Use DOP Madeirense for the still Porto Santo wines unless a wine-specific source documents DOP Madeira; do not collapse the two protected designations.
statement: The research-handoff formulation that Listrão dos Profetas and Vinho da Corda dos Profetas fall under the Madeira D.O. as though Madeira and Madeirense were one appellation is rejected.

resolution_needed: Do not merge Caracol with Palomino/Listán or another grape until a primary scientific or official ampelographic source resolves the relationship.
statement: Caracol is retained as a separate grape identity; the research handoff's suggested clone or synonym relationship to Listán/Cedrés is not sufficiently supported for CARTA authority in this pass.
Clos du Tue-Boeuf is a Loire estate in Les Montils whose proprietors are Thierry and Zoë Puzelat; Louis/Dressner records 14 hectares plus purchased fruit and certified-organic farming.

The 2024 Le Brin de Chèvre is a Vin de France white composed of 90% Menu Pineau and 10% Petit Meslier from neighboring parcels planted in 1937 and 1950, with later massale-selection replantings contributing part of the wine.

For 2024 Le Brin de Chèvre, Bowler documents manual harvest, direct pressing, spontaneous native-yeast fermentation without sulfur in large oak, about a year in used demi-muids and Burgundy barrels, no racking, occasional lees stirring, and unfined/unfiltered bottling with a minute sulfur addition.

Le Brin de Chèvre is presented in the verified 2024 trade record as Vin de France, while INAO describes Cheverny blanc as a Sauvignon-and-Chardonnay blend; CARTA keeps physical location and wine classification separate.

resolution_needed: Do not describe the verified 1937/1950 Brin de Chèvre parcels as pre-phylloxera without separate evidence for surviving pre-phylloxera vine material.
statement: The research handoff's description of the 1937 and 1950 Le Brin de Chèvre plantings as pre-phylloxera is rejected; those planting dates are twentieth-century and do not support that characterization.
JONATA was established in 1998 when a group acquired the 600-acre property; E. Stanley Kroenke later invested and became sole owner in 2008, and Matt Dees was recruited for the first vintage in 2004.

JONATA states that its estate vineyard became officially certified organic in 2022 and identifies the estate vineyard location as Ballard Canyon AVA within Santa Ynez Valley in Santa Barbara County, California.
TTB lists Ballard Canyon as an American Viticultural Area established October 2, 2013, located in Santa Barbara County and within the Santa Ynez Valley AVA.

Santa Barbara County can serve as a county appellation of origin on U.S. wine labels, but it is not an American Viticultural Area; Decanter records Santa Barbara County as the appellation for the 2021 Todos.

JONATA describes Todos as an annual estate mosaic whose blend changes with vineyard and vintage, supporting one persistent Todos wine identity with vintage-scoped composition rather than separate identities for each recipe.

The 2022 Todos is documented as 70% Syrah, 15% Petite Sirah, 10% Cabernet Sauvignon, 3% Merlot and 2% miscellaneous red and white varieties from the JONATA Estate, aged 20 months in 35% new and 65% neutral French oak, with 2,545 cases produced.

resolution_needed: Use JONATA's first-party history: estate established in 1998; Kroenke became sole owner in 2008.
statement: The research-handoff assertions that the JONATA site was purchased in 2000 and that Stan Kroenke was sole owner from the estate's founding are rejected.

resolution_needed: Do not infer destemming or tank-fermentation details for Todos from generic California practice; use wine- or vintage-specific evidence.
statement: The research handoff's assumed conventional destemmed/tank-fermentation description for Todos is not accepted as CARTA authority because JONATA's verified materials do not establish those details.
